risks: Minimal. Risks are that individual reports feel punitive to faculty and that rated comments identify residents; reports go only to the faculty member and comments are rated without names.
consent: Faculty are told at the September meeting how comments will be sampled and reported, and may ask not to receive individual reports; residents are informed through the program newsletter. No additional data are collected from either group.
data: Comment text is extracted without names or dates; the key linking comments to faculty for individual reports is held by the program administrator; results are reported at program level only.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: resident gender is analysed because vaguer comments for women residents are reported elsewhere; international medical graduates are a second group of concern, but the program will not create a new identifier for them and notes this as a limitation.
effectiveness: Success is a sustained shift in actionable comments with no fall in forms completed and no widening gender gap.
efficiency: Under 30 minutes of rating a week and 20 minutes of each monthly meeting.
costs: No direct costs; staff time within existing roles.
grants: None needed; a positive result could support a regional medical education innovation grant for spread.
partnerships: Chief residents (measurement), program administrator (extraction), two residents from the program's wellness committee (report design) and the competence committee chair.
rebPath: Determined to be quality improvement not requiring REB review by the education research office (EDU-QI-2026-19); a later publication follows SQUIRE 2.0 and the journal's QI policy.
limitations: One program; raters not fully blinded; gender taken from program records.
summary: Minimal-risk QI with private faculty reports, name-free rating and a pre-specified gender breakdown.
